articleTitle: Simulation model for generic phased array antennas for microwave landing systems
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: A generic antenna model which simulates various MLS antenna configurations is described. The performance of the user specified antenna is analyzed using the MLS type parameters such as Effective Radiated Power (ERP), Mean Angle Error (MAE), Filtered Raw Angle (FRA), Control Motion Noise (CMN) and Path Following Error (PFE). Other parameters such as beamwidth, beamshape, dynamic sidelobe level and sidelobe structure are available from the static pattern and dynamic pattern generated by the model at a given point in space. The model was validated using the antenna range data for the MLS-400T azimuth antenna.

articleTitle: An efficient network approach for spectral domain green's functions
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: The direct way of evaluating spectral domain Green's functions in the spectral domain moment method is to expand electromagnetic wave modes in each dielectric layer and match the boundary conditions at layer interfaces to obtain unknown coefficients. For multi-layer structures, this leads to a very lengthy derivation process. In [1], an immitance approach is proposed to derive the spectral domain Green's function for planar electric currents in printed transmission lines of two dimensional problems. In [2], a set of formulations are derived to evaluate Green's functions by an iteration process. In [3], a dyadic spectral domain Green's function for single layer grounded dielectrics was derived for electric currents and a corresponding network displayed for this structure. However, the Green's function was still derived from the Maxwell's equations and boundary conditions.

articleTitle: RCS of small aircraft at HF frequencies
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: This paper investigates the RCS of two aircraft in the HF frequency range, for a plane wave incident on the nose of the aircraft with the electric field oriented vertically. The “generic aircraft” is a simplified aircraft geometry which demonstrates the basic features of aircraft RCS in the HF band. Good agreement is obtained between the measured RCS, that obtained by wire-grid modelling, and that from an FDTD model. A method is given for deriving an FDTD cell model of a fully three-dimensional aircraft such as the Navajo. The RCS of the Navajo aircraft obtained by wire-grid modelling is compared with that from FDTD, and differences are found that are associated with the staircased approximation. The RCS of the 10 m Navajo to 30 MHz is very similar to the RCS of the 30 m generic aircraft up to 10 MHz.

articleTitle: Scale modelling of an HP log-periodic array antenna for ground wave propagation
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: Recently, a number of Vertical Log Periodic Array (VLPA) configurations suitable for Ground Wave Radar applications have been developed. Their radiation characteristics in the HF band are calculated numerically. Scale models are built for VLPA with dipole or monopole elements and tested in the University of Manitoba's anechoic chamber. Using an 1:600 scaling factor, requires the wires to be etched on a printed circuit. Comparisons of numerically evaluated radiation patterns of HF designs with measured ones of microwave-sized scale models are made. The effects of high scaling factor, use of flat wires on the VLPA, limited ground size, and use of complete model image are illustrated. This study identifies the validity of scale modelling measurements under the above mentioned conditions.

articleTitle: Performing PSK demodulation using six-ports
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: A six-port junction is used to perform demodulation of PSK signals directly at RF frequencies. The proposed direct phase demodulator is capable of demodulating various digital modulations such as BPSK, QPSK, etc. The hardware imperfections are readily eliminated by software. Due to the absence of the frequency conversion stages the receiver becomes very simple. Measurements have been performed at mm-wave frequencies (40GHz) on DBPSK demodulation. The results outline a promising new direct digital receiver.

articleTitle: RADARSAT SAR antenna RF design
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: The synthetic aperture radar (SAR) antenna on-board the Canadian remote sensing satellite, RADARSAT, is a large deployable planar array (1.5m × 15m) [1], [2]. It provides a set of selectable pseudo-trapezoidal elevation beam shapes (see figure 1–1) which afford flexible coverage within a 500 km wide accessibility region, which runs parallel to, and to the side of, the orbital plane of the spacecraft. In order to achieve the desired SAR image quality, the antenna is required to meet stringent gain requirements, while maintaining sufficiently low sidelobe levels, as well as sharp beam fall-off slopes, consistent with low SAR ambiguity ratios. The azimuth plane radiation pattern is a pencil beam with tightly controlled beamwidth to preserve the SAR along-track resolution. The required cross-track resolution determines the SAR antenna frequency bandwidth specification of ±10 MHz at 5.3 GHz, and up to ±16 MHz for finer resolution beams. Pulse distortion within the frequency band is controlled through phase and amplitude pulseerror specifications, and RF coherence over each SAR integration period, which is of the order of 1 second, is imposed by aperture synthesis error requirements on the antenna short-term stability. The design of the SAR antenna under these constraints constituted a challenge. Section 2 describes briefly the RF design and the major trade-offs behind the different design choices. Section 3 gives a brief overview of the design and analysis methods used to design the SAR antenna and predict its performance. Section 4 compares the performance predictions with measured data so as to validate the analysis and software tools.

articleTitle: An accurate dispersion model for shielded microstrip lines
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: A dispersion model for shielded microstrip lines is given here for the first time. This model is valid for a wide range of values of frequency, geometrical parameters and of relative dielectric constants. Unlike previous models for open microstrip lines, the inflection frequency of the dispersion curve has been shown to be a polynomial of the frequency at which the quasi TEM mode of the microstrip couples with the lowest order Transverse Electric mode. This dispersion model yields excellent accuracy with respect to numerical techniques. Also presented is a detailed analysis of asymptotic behaviour of dispersion in shielded microstrip lines. This model will be useful in time and frequency domain analysis of various shielded microstrip discontinuities, components, resonators and VLSI packagings. Dispersion in open microstrips can be treated as a special case of this model.

articleTitle: A circularly polarized dielectric guide antenna with a single slot feed
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: Recently, dielectric resonator antennas (DA) have been proposed as alternative radiators to the popular microstrip patch [1]-[3]. They have been demonstrated to possess characteristics similar to those of microstrip patches, i.e. low profile and compatibility with planar integration technologies, both desirable properties for future active phased arrays. However, they also have advantages over microstrip patches; a wider operational impedance bandwidth [3] and higher efficiency resulting from the nonexistence of conducting and surface wave losses [4]. These properties also make the DA a good candidate for millimeter wave applications.

articleTitle: Some aspects of dielectric lens design
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: Some aspects of synthesising and analysing dielectric lens antenna are considered in this paper. The suitability of the spherical and shaped lenses to generate simultaneous multiple beams is investigated using the analysis technique developed.

articleTitle: Multiple beam antenna concepts for satellite communications
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: Multiple beam antennas (MBA) for satellite communications usually provide a contiguous coverage over a specified field-of-view by using high gain overlapping spot beams. The common design objective for all MBAs is to maximize the minimum gain within the coverage region. If the MBA has uniform beams arranged in a hexagonal grid, the minimum gain occurs at the triple beam cross-over and the gain variation within the coverage region is typically around 4 dB. The trades for gain optimization are often coupled with consideration such as (a) low sidelobe levels for frequency reuse or for minimizing interference effects (b) minimizing the number of beams to reduce the antenna complexity (c) power and traffic allocation flexibility and (d) size and mass constraints. Antenna designs and beamforming network (BFN) concepts suitable for MBAs are discussed in this paper including design examples.

articleTitle: Measurement of microwave permittivity and surface resistivity by using open-ended coaxial lines
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: In this presentation a detailed discussion on the measurement of microwave permittivity of dielectric slabs and surface resistivity of thin films are given. A new needle-type coaxial probe with improved performance is also described and evaluated.

articleTitle: Potentially hazardous near-field electromagnetic emanations from handheld transceivers
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: The use of handheld transmitter-receiver units by the military, commercial users and others has proliferated in the last ten years. This paper presents calculations that indicate with reasonable accuracy that these units, although excluded from ANSI C95.1-1982 protection guidelines, may be a radiation hazard. The transmitters generate between one and five watts of radio frequency power, operate on HF, VHF and UHF bands; and use short spiral (rubber ducky) antennas. They are held near the face during transmissions. Although no calculations or measurements give unequivocal values for the electromagnetic energy in the near field, energy densities in the induction fields (within the head of the user) may be an order of magnitude greater than ANSI protection guidelines.

articleTitle: Radiation from a slot located in a face of a rounded wedge
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: In modeling antennas and their surroundings, or complex radar targets, configurations consisting of wedge structures are often involved. In several cases the wedge can be truncated close to its edge, and the truncation can also be characterized by a rounded boundary, even with a variable radius of curvature. This problem cannot be easily treated analytically; as a matter of fact only the simple problem of a perfectly conducting rounded wedge with constant curvature excited by a plane wave [1] or by a current line [2] have been investigated.

publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]

articleTitle: Array Factor Considerations for Rectangular Dielectric Resonator Antennas
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: As telecommunications and radar systems are increasingly being designed to operate at higher and higher frequencies in the millimetre wave band, antenna designers have looked arrays, with feed networks based in microwave integrated circuit (MIC) technology, to meet the antenna requirements of these systems. Most of the research and design into arrays for millimetre wave applications has focused on various configurations of microstrip patch antennas (MPAs). Unfortunately, this technology may be pushed to its limits at higher frequencies, where conductor losses of the metal patch and surface wave losses become more serious problems. As well, MPAs are inherently narrowband devices, typically offering a bandwidth of 1 to 2 % of the operating frequency, making them unsuitable for many wideband telecommunications applications. One is left with the need for an antenna array element which is efficient and wideband at higher frequencies, and is easily integrated with MIC subsystem components.

articleTitle: Radiation patterns of slotted prolate spheroidal antennas
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: The characteristics of a prolate spheroidal antenna, excited by a rotationally symmetric narrow slot, have been discussed by Wait [1]. Sinha and MacPhie[2] have discussed the admittance characteristics of an antenna system consisting of two symmetrically center-fed prolate spheroids in parallel configuration. Ciric and Cooray[3] have further investigated such two spheroidal dipole antennas in an arbitrary configuration. It seems, however, that discussions or formulations treating an asymmetrically fed slot antenna on prolate spheroids have not been carried out, and little quantities are available for such excitation. The work presented in this paper is concerned with such a case of spheroidal antennas.

articleTitle: A convenient expression of spectral green's function for multilayer media
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: For a multilayer medium, the complex images give a simple but accurate approximation to the spatial Green's functions when transformed from the known analytical spectral Green's functions. For a medium with many layers, the latter are tedious to derive. This paper sidesteps the problem by evaluating directly from the constituent simple transmission matrices of an equivalent cascading transmission line. The matrices themselves now become the convenient spectral Green's functions.

articleTitle: Advanced satcom antenna design tradeoffs
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: This paper describes parametric relationships that affect the design of high gain multibeam antennas, discusses tradeoffs, and presents optimized performance of two candidate antennas for wide-angle coverage Advanced Satcom: an aperiodic array with suppressed grating lobes and reduced number of elements, and a side-fed offset Cassegrain system with low scan loss. Given basic performance requirements such as the edge-of-coverage gain and the size of the coverage area, we shall determine parameters such as the antenna directivity and beamwidth, aperture diameter, radiating element diameter, number of elements, scan loss, number of beams, etc. Rather than performing a singe-point design which provides limited information, we shall obtain functional relationships spanning a range of vlaues.

articleTitle: Model of a microwave oven with focalizing antennas
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: In this paper we study the mathematical modelling of a domestic microwave oven with incorporated metallic bars. These bars act like antennas. They are powered by the microwave energy that excites the oven and transmit the energy to the surface of the lossy load (see figure 1). The calculation of the field inside the cavity and of the external characteristics of the cavity as seen by the source guide starts with Maxwell's equations and was curried out by simultaneously using the Finite Element Method (F.E.M.) and integral field equations. The goal of this type of oven is to concentrate the maximum amount of energy into the load in order to use the oven to its best advantage. In our study, we have considered that the metal bars are perfect conductors; the choice of their positions is vary important, so as to keep the coefficient of reflection as low as possible.

articleTitle: Accurate determination of the s-matrix of a circular waveguide polarizer module
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: A Moment Method analysis of a typical circular waveguide polarizer module is described in this paper. The method uses complete sets of entire domain basis and testing functions which provide a high accuracy in the predicted complex scattered fields. Precision design of polarizers can be achieved using this algorithm. Predicted results for a design example are presented.

articleTitle: Visualization of geometries using MATLAB code
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: This paper will present codes whose function is to pre- and post-process information used by the Numerical Electromagnetic Code Basic Scattering code and the Richmond Thin Wire code. The processor uses the MATLAB environment for the fundamental graphical functions. The Basic Scattering Code uses the principles of ray optics as well as the geometrical theory of diffraction. The Richmond code uses a method of moments technique to generate a solution for the scattered field. The pre/post-processor can allow the user to view the input geometry as well as to produce plots of the radiation patterns. Other features include ray tracing in the case of the ray optics code and current magnitude in the case of the thin wire code.

articleTitle: A dual polarized antenna for digital radio broadcast
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: The digital radio program is anticipated to be broadcast simultaneously through the Satellite and Terrestrial Stations. To receive the program the ground antenna should have adequate gain for both transmitters. The challenging problem is with the mobile antennas that must maintain its gain during the operation. The broadcast will be in the L-Band, around 1.45–1.5 GHz, and circularly polarized for the satellite and vertically polarized for Terrestrial Stations. The required mobile antenna should therefore handle both polarizations.

articleTitle: Analysis of slot-coupled microstrip structures using the transmission line matrix method
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: In this paper, the analysis of slot-coupled microstrip structures is considered. Typical methods applied to the analysis of this class of problem include: analytic techniques such as modal-field analysis [1], cavity models [2]; and the numerical solution of integral-equation formulations [3]. The Transmission Line Matrix (TLM) method is a general numerical technique for obtaining an approximate solution of the time-dependent Maxwell's equations in the presence of complex environments [4]. During the past few years, we have been developing a general purpose electromagnetic simulation program based on the three-dimensional symmetric-condensed TLM model [5]. Previous applications of this general purpose simulation program include the analysis of half-space problems, and characterization of the radar-cross-section of finite-sized conducting and material objects [6]. In this paper, the application of the general purpose TLM simulation program to the analysis of slot-coupled microstrip structures is considered.

articleTitle: Noncontact voltage measurement in microwave integrated circuits
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: The ability to noninvasively measure high frequency signals at the internal points of an integrated circuit is important in performing diagnostics of current high speed microelectronics. Conventional measurement techniques rely on direct electrical contact with a point on the circuit being monitored. These measurements are limited to predefined test points and are difficult to perform without disturbing the circuit's normal operation. To overcome this problem, several noninvasive techniques have been developed such as electron beam probing [1], electro-optic probing [2], capacitive and inductive near-field imaging [3], [4] and photoconductive sampling [5]. These methods often require complex calibration procedures, may be unable to provide repeatable accurate magnitude measurements, have low spatial or temporal resolution, or must be performed in vacuum. In the last decade, scanned probe microscopes (SPMs) have been used for microelectronic diagnostics [6], [7]. The operating principle of these instruments relies on sensing the mechanical deflection of a small probe to extract the desired signal from the structure under test. These techniques promise both high spatial and temporal resolution. This paper presents a heterodyne electrostatic force SPM technique [8] which is capable of providing accurate noninvasive measurement of high frequency signals. A nulling technique enables measurement to be made without complex probe positioning or calibration.

articleTitle: Development of 20 and 30 Ghz MMICS intended for personal communications, phased array antenna systems
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: Future satellite based, personal communications systems operating in the 20/30 GHz frequency range will require small and reliable RF components capable of being manufactured in large quantities. Suitcase sized terminals are expected to be available and phased array antennas appear to be an attractive way of realizing the necessary planar antenna configuration. Integrated circuit technologies such as MMICs have the size, quantity and performance characteristics required for the RF electronics but new approaches to integrated packaging are also necessary if costs are to be minimized. Such integrated packages must, of course, include the special needs of the antenna and associated feed networks.

articleTitle: A travelling wave front-end MMIC chip for an optical receiver
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: It is shown that the equivalent input noise current density of a travelling wave front-end of an optical receiver can be improved by using a combination of large gate line matching impedance and series inductive tuning. A MMIC travelling wave front-end utilizing these design considerations is experimentally shown to have a 8 GHz bandwidth and an equivalent input noise current density 8 pA/√Hz.

articleTitle: Some novel designs to minimize the angular sensitivity of FSS structures
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: To reduce the angular and polarization sensitivity of FSS structures, various novel geometries such as double layered periodic structures composed of open or shorted square rings are proposed as cell elements. Results are presented to demonstrate the feasibility of removing the angular constraints upon the “reflective characteristics” of a resonating FSS. Logical steps that led to the proposed geometry will be pointed out as well.

articleTitle: Chirped grating as a demultiplexer: Analysis and synthesis using coupled mode theory
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: We study the performance of a chirped sinusoidal surface relief grating in an optical waveguide as a wavelength demultiplexer by means of local normal mode theory. Linear chirp and contrapropagating guided-to-guided mode coupling is considered in phase synchronism. Two first-order differential coupled-mode equations with variable coefficients give approximate solutions for the coupling of the contrapropagating modes. Considerations include TE and TM mode coupling.

articleTitle: The EHF personal communications portable offset reflector antenna system
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: This paper describes the development of the EHF offset reflector antenna system for Personal Communications, Picoterminals. The picoterminal antenna system is an experimental unit designed for personal communications via satellite from any stationary location at an EHF band of 20/30 GHz. The antenna system consists of mechanically steered linearly polarized offset paraboloid reflector that uses a shared aperture for both Tx/Rx bands and fits into a small briefcase of 350 × 250 × 500 mm size. The numerical modelling of the antenna system is completed and the experimental investigation is currently underway.

articleTitle: CROSSED slot coupled microstrip “magic-t”
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: Advancements in microstrip technologies have made possible the development of many miniature multilayered integrated devices, for various antenna and microstrip circuitry applications. The use of a coupling slot (aperture) in these devices is a recent method utilized for coupling electromagnetic energy from one substrate layer to another. This technique generally involves the use of a rectangular slot, perpendicularly oriented to the feedline, cut in the ground plane between the layers. In this paper coupling by use of inclined and crossed rectangular slots is investigated, with particular emphasis placed on their use in enhancement to the performance of a newly developed microstrip “Magic-T”. Results show good agreement with theoretical prediction and successfully demonstrate that coupling strength; can be varied by changing the angle of a single inclined slot, and can be increased by use of a two slot crossed pattern. Improvement in the operational band width can also be obtained by using two crossed slots. The results should be useful for other applications in multilayered integrated microstrip configurations.

articleTitle: An approximate complex image green's function for a truncated dielectric substrate
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: In MIC's and printed antennas the dielectric substrates always have finite extent. Rigorous analysis of the truncation effects requires the solution of an integral equation with MoM. This is usually numerically intense especially for 3-D structures. In this paper the truncation effects are incorporated directly in an approximate Green's function. The Characteristic Green's Function (CGF) technique is combined with the complex images method to derive the Green's function. The derived Green's function exhibits excellent agreement with the available rigorous MoM solution of the problem.

articleTitle: Shaped reflectors employing customized feeds: Novel designs for identical coverage at dual bands
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: Fixed coverage contour beam antennas for geo-stationary satellites can be obtained employing a shaped reflector illuminated by a single feed. Needless to emphasize, this offers a highly attractive alternative to reflector antennas illuminated by an array of feeds. The stringent specifications on the gain slope within the coverage contour and the isolation outside the coverage contour call for suitable reflector surface synthesis procedure driven by a precision analysis technique. Furthermore, when such specifications must be obtained simultaneously at two widely separated bands, the feed reflector relationship must be duly considered.

articleTitle: Future communications satellite antennas
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: The conventional design approach to provide a shaped beam antenna pattern has been to illuminate a paraboloid reflector with a multielement feed array. The beam shaping is achieved by selection of the size and placement of the feed elements in the focal plane of the reflector, and the excitation coefficient which drive the elements. Recent developments at Space Systems/Loral have proven the benefits of a shaped reflector antenna design approach, which uses a single feed to illuminate the shaped reflector surface. The following paragraphs will detail the improvements which have been realized, and will discuss implementation of a shaped reflector for the TEMPO communication satellite. At the end of the paper, future improvements will be discussed.

articleTitle: A 42 GHz linear array of active aperture-coupled microstrip patch antennas
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: With the current trend in communications towards extremely high frequencies and minimized system dimensions microstrip patch antennas have the potential to replace reflector antennas as the radiator of choice in certain applications due to their small size, ease of integration, and conformability. However, at millimeter-wave frequencies, significant microstrip transmission line loss occurs. This loss severely affects microstrip antenna gain performance. The transmission line losses can be overcome by the integration of amplifiers throughout the feed network to form an active antenna.

articleTitle: Loop antenna with a parasitic element
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: The loop antenna is well known as a fundamental element that radiates a linearly polarized wave. Recently, some unique properties have been discussed for a loop antenna capable of radiating a circularly polarized wave (CPW) [1]-[4]. CPW radiation is obtained using two perturbation elements on the loop.

articleTitle: A simple cavity model for radiation analysis of unidirectional dielectric radiator (UDR)
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: In this paper, a simple cavity model is presented for the theoretical prediction of the radiation patterns of unidirectional dielectric radiator (UDR). The antenna structure is first modeled as a non-radiative dielectric waveguide (NRD) resonator, the electromagnetic fields at the radiating aperture of the antenna structure are then determined for the calculation of the radiation fields and patterns of the UDR antenna. A good agreement between the calculations and measurements shows the validity of the analysis model.

articleTitle: Procedure for the computation of singular integrals in method of moments
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: An efficient method for the evaluation of singular integrals appearing in the analysis of electromagnetic scattering by arbitrarily shaped bodies modelled by triangular patches is presented. The derived expressions which are in closed form involve algebraic functions whose evaluation is not cumbersome and thus facilitate the ease of computations. In the proposed analysis, the Green's function is approximated using only the two terms of Taylor series.

articleTitle: SAR distributions of non-uniformly coated interstitial applicators for medical hyperthermia and radiometric imaging
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: The benefit of hyperthermia as an adjuvant treatment to brachytherapy in the treatment of breast cancer and other accessible tumours has been widely documented [1]. Results obtained by a variety of researchers have been very consistent. A recent review paper shows an improvement in complete response rates from 37% for radiation alone to 63% for combined radiation and hyperthermia treatment [2]. The objective of the hyperthermia treatment is to raise the tumour temperature to 43°–55°C while keeping the temperature of surrounding tissue below 44°C. The elevated temperature impairs many cellular functions and studies indicate that this greatly increases the effectiveness of chemotherapy and radiation treatments.

articleTitle: Measurement results of indoor radio channel at 37.2GHz
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: Intensive investigations of the millimeter waves spectrum are stimulated by the requirements of large bandwidth adapted to the high bit rate of the future wireless LAN. This paper deals with experimental results obtained for the narrowband and wideband indoor radio channels at 37.2 GHz. CW results are obtained using two kinds of transmission antennas, omnidirectional and directional Under LOS condition, distance-power law exponent is found to be lower than free space condition, walls playing a major role on the sustaining of high level signal. Large scale and small scale variations extracted form the original data are shown to follow, respectively, log-normal and Rice distributions. The observed wideband impulse response has delay spread extending over a range up to 40 ns and a maximum rms value of about 16 ns.

articleTitle: Design of a coplanar waveguide branch-line coupler for superconductive circuits
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: A coplanar waveguide (CPW) is an attractive transmission line for superconducting applications because the presence of the CPW ground and centre strip in the same plane eliminates the need for via holes. These via holes may break the fragile substrate, lanthanum aluminate, most often used with superconductors.

articleTitle: Perturbation feedback method for parallel dielectric rectangular directional coupler
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: Parallel dielectric waveguides are used as optical directional couplers. In this paper for two identical rectangular parallel dielectric waveguides, the propagation constants are calculated by the perturbation feedback method.

articleTitle: Microwave method of assessing the quality of high temperature superconductor thin films
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: A simple cavity resonator is described for measuring surface resistance (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>) of high temperature superconductor (HTS) thin films. The cavity is a one-half wavelength of WR-28 waveguide with the HTS forming a short across one end. A choke ring reduces the need for low resistance contact. Quantitative R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> measurements can be made over the range of 10 mΩ to 500 mΩ at liquid nitrogen temperature and at the operating frequency of 31 Ghz.

articleTitle: Modeling of antennas with lumped impedance loading using FDTD
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: The finite-difference time-domain technique (FDTD) is used to model electromagnetic systems with lumped elements. The FDTD equations are modified to account for the presence of lumped elements such as R, L, and C and current or voltage sources inside the grid. FDTD equations that include nonlinear elements, i.e., diodes and transistors arc derived.

articleTitle: Modelling of human exposure to various sources of 60 Hz magnetic fields
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: The knowledge of induced currents in the human body from exposure to various sources of power line frequency magnetic field is important in the assessment of potential health hazards. This paper briefly outlines methods of computations of magnetic fields from sources such as high-voltage transmission lines or other line current-carrying conductors, and from small appliances. To compute the induced currents, the impedance method is used for realistic models of human body. Differences in level and distribution of induced currents are discussed for a uniform magnetic field, that in the vicinity of a three phase power-line representing exposure of a lineman, and a person using a hand-held appliance such as a hair-dryer.

articleTitle: A novel microstrip phased array antenna for wide angle coverage in mobile satellite communications
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: A slotted microstrip patch antenna has been developed which provides a broader beam compared to a conventional square or rectangular patch. Dual frequency operation was achieved using a stacked configuration of the elements with a parasitic top patch (a solid patch without any slots) above a slotted patch which was driven with the help of an equal power splitter to give a right handed circular polarization. A bandwidth of 9% is achieved for a VSWR of less than 1.7. A planar array has been developed using the slotted patch to provide a wide angle coverage from 25° to 55° above the horizon with a variation of 2 dB in gain. This paper presents the measured patterns, optimized impedance match of the single element and the simulated results of the array at the mid-band frequency.

articleTitle: Capacitance calculation and its application to integrated circuits interconnections
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: In [1], a new method has been developed to minimize the cost and memory requirements of the integral equation method (IEM) for the capacitance calculation of multiconductor system embedded in a homogeneous dielectric medium. In this paper, the method has been extended to the calculation of the capacitance matrix for integrated circuits applications.

articleTitle: Field patterns inside a boxed microstrip line
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: A new Full Wave Finite Difference (FWFD) is proposed which is capable of evaluating field patterns of guided wave structures simultaneously and efficiently. Unlike the traditional finite difefrence methods, its formulation is based on all six vector field components.

articleTitle: A generalized scattering matrix for cascaded waveguide junctions
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: The equivalence principle and the moment method are used to present a solution for the scattering matrix when a number of waveguide junctions (more than one) are considered together in a cascade. This solution presents each two consecutive waveguide junctions by their scattering matrix. The overall scattering matrix of a cascade of waveguide junctions can be obtained by the multiplication of the scattering matrices of each two consecutive junctions. Numerical results are presented graphically for a waveguide with four junctions.

articleTitle: Adaptive antenna system (AAS) using a six-port module
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: Generally, an Adaptative Antenna System (AAS) controls the beam shape and steering. AAS's tasks are essentially to find the direction of an emitter and to reduce sidelobe levels of the antenna pattern in the direction of interferences. AAS finds application in radars [1] and in mobile or wireless indoor communications [2]. The AAS contains coherent receivers giving relative phase and magnitude and polarization of the incoming wave field sampled by radiators array [1]. Coherent receivers are either In Phase and Quadrature phase detectors using mixers and local oscillator, or either six-port systems using power detectors [3]. In this last case [3], AAS calibration was performed without radiator array. This paper presents a new calibration procedure of the overall AAS taking into account coupling factor of each radiator of the AAS.

articleTitle: Application of polarimetric synthetic aperture radar to a ship wake in simulation
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: The analysis presented in this paper provides a polarimetric observation over the Kelvin's wake sensed by a SAR in a numerical simulation. A computer simulation of L band SAR images of surface ship wakes is described and the results analysed. The model accounts for the perturbation in the fluid by the ship and the influence of the sea in calm wind conditions. The fluctuations of the Kelvin's waves alter the local angle of incidence, so the simulation combines the sea and wake heights and slopes. The results of simulation depend on the parameters of the ship, the SAR, and also the geometry of the observation.

articleTitle: A new broad band ring coupled triangular mcirostrip antenna
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: A new ring coupled triangular microstrip antenna has been investigated experimentally. The measured bandwidth of the proposed antenna is obtained 309 MHz (7.14% at fo = 4.33 GHz), which is 4 times the band width of the corresponding triangular patch antenna. The gain of the antenna is 3 dB and cross polar level is better than 12 dB within the impedance bandwidth of 7%.

articleTitle: Analysis of aircraft landing system integrity — The microwave landing system
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: Rick Cassell has 19 years experience working with MLS. He has extensive experience in analyzing MLS integrity and continuity of service. He has worked for the last ten years as an advisor to the U.S. representative on the International Civil Aviation Organization All Weather Operations Panel. He has a Bachelor's Degree in Electrical Engineering from Villanova University.

articleTitle: Stochastic reconstruction of dielectric permittivities with multiple illuminations
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: Numerical results presented recently show that the stochastic inversion method is one of the promising spatial domain methods for reconstructing dielectric permittivities, especially in a noise contaminated environment [1],[2]. The stochastic inversion algorithm is developed based on statistical considerations, with the generated reconstructions and the noise modelled in terms of stochastic or random processes. Under the assumption that the random variables for both the reconstructions and the noise in the scattered field are uncorrelated, the algorithm seeks the best estimate of the reconstructed values iteratively. Computer simulations have shown that, for relatively simple scatter geometries, the application of the stochastic inversion allows us to obtain microwave images of high resolution even when only one incident wave illumination is used and even when the measured field contains a high level of noise. However, for more complex geometries, as in other spatial domain methods, one illumination is not enough for developing satisfactory pictures due to the ill-posedness inherent in the inverse scattering problems. In order to get reliable microwave images, multi-view techniques have to be used. In this paper, the stochastic inversion algorithm is further developed by using multiple illuminations, with transmitters and receivers located around the investigation region. Numerical results show that a dielectric cylinder of a cross-sectional dimension of Λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/2, with a relative permittivity of ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> = 3, can be well reconstructed even for the measured field data containing high level of noise.

articleTitle: A general method for the computation of electromagnetic scattering problems
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: Electromagnetic field scattering problems can be solved by either an analytical or numerical method. With the advancement of computers, the numerical method has lately received a lot of attention. However, in some aspects, an analytical method can still offer certain advantages over the numerical approach. This includes a better physical insight into the problems and a better computational efficiency for specific cases. Moreover, the analytical technique can be applied to formulate a problem which can be solved numerically using, for example, the moment method.

articleTitle: Design aspects of uniplanar microwave and millimeterwa VE hybrid and monolithic circuits considering finite metal thickness
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: Propagation characteristics of uniplanar structures consisting of slotline and coplanar waveguide are studied using an enhanced spectral-domain approach. Numerical results are presented for design consideration of various slotlines and CPWs on alumina and GaAs substrates. Effects of structural parameters on characteristics are discussed.

articleTitle: Conical-cylindrical HELIX for the AMT aircraft communication system
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: The CAL AMT-100 system provides communications capabilities for an aircraft. Via the Inmarsat series of L-band satellites, voice or data facilities (phone, fax etc.) are available globally on demand. The antenna for the system (Fig. 1) is housed in a tail-mounted radome, and is mechanically scanned in two dimensions to track the satellite.

articleTitle: A hybrid finite integral technique / method of moments formulation for the analysis of cavity-backed aperture antennas
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: A numerical algorithm has been developed for the analysis of cavity-backed spiral and slot antennas in a ground plane, in which the cavities may be arbitrarily shaped and may have discrete rotational symmetry. It also permits the treatment of inhomogeneously loaded cavities. The finite integral technique (FIT) is used to model the fields in the cavity [1]. The FIT is similar in many respects to the finite element method (FEM), but is based on the direct simulation of the integral form of Maxwell's equations. Both the FIT and the FEM have advantages over volume integral equation techniques due to the sparse nature of the resulting matrix equation. For both formulations, the inhomogeneous volume is divided into small piecewise-homogeneous elements, which are tetrahedra in this work. The interior fields are coupled directly to the exterior fields through a surface integral equation in the aperture that is solved using the method of moments (MoM).

articleTitle: Radiation by an axial slot on a dielectric-coated eccentric conducting circular cylinder
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: The radiation characteristics of the eccentrically coated axial slot cylindrical antenna is examined. The boundary value method is employed to obtain the solution with the aid of the addition theorem of the Bessel functions. The resulting dual infinite series involved in the solution is then truncated to generate numerical results. Several examples showing the antenna radiation characteristics corresponding to some interesting geometries of the coated slot cylindrical antenna are illustrated.

articleTitle: Full-wave analysis of microstrip structures integrated with nonradiating networks
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: The analysis of microstrip structures has received a great deal of attention from many different researchers [1],[2]. Of particular interest is the Mixed Potential Integral Equation (MPIE) formulation as presented by Mosig and Gardiol [1]. This method exploits the continuity equation to develop an integral equation in terms of both surface current and surface charge densities. The solution scheme that ensues approximates the current using overlapping basis functions, providing a smooth source distribution. In general, good results are obtained even with a coarse segmentation of the conducting surface.

articleTitle: Hybridization and generalization of numerical methods: Application to MMP3D
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: The original ideas which lead to the development of MMP-3D are still very much in use. However during the past years, there has been some recent improvements which lead to both the hybridization and generalization of the method. In particular, there has been a generalization for the sources or basis functions, to allow the computation of special geometries. Also, a combination with line theory has lead to a new type of boundary equations to allow the computation of fields going through shieldings. The general theoretical aspects will be the main purpose of this paper.

articleTitle: Propagation characteristics of composite nonradiative dielectric waveguides considering dielectric and OHMIC losses
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: Complex propagation characteristics of composite nonradiative dielectric waveguides (NRD) are presented. Dielectric and ohmic losses are considered in this hybrid mode analysis based on the frequency-domain transmission-line matrix approach. Numerical results of mode dispersion characteristics indicate that a class of complex modes in both lossless and lossy cases may be supported in the composite dielectric structures under certain conditions. It is further confirmed that a single mode transmission becomes somehow impossible in the composite high-permittivity NRD-guides involving air gaps. Some interesting phenomenons such as the vortical mode pattern are discussed.

articleTitle: Bootlace lens feed for a sidelobe canceller
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: The design and measurements of a Bootlace lens feed for an auxiliary sidelobe canceller array are discussed in this paper. The sidelobe canceller is an array of 8 pyramidal horns, each fed by a phase-matched low noise receiver, as shown in Fig. 1. These active elements are connected to the output or array ports of the lens. The Rotman variation of the Bootlace lens, depicted in Fig. 2, is implemented here. The input or beam ports of the lens are directed to an adaptive processor where the appropriate beam, in the vicinity of the jammer, is selected. The advantages of having beams generated by a lens are that the directions of the beams are invariant to change in frequency and each beam has the gain of the full array aperture. The frequency invariant property is the result of path length constraint from the beam port to the radiated wavefront, a feature of the synthesis procedure. The lens is required to produce a weakly tapered distribution across the array ports over the frequency band from 8.5 to 10.0 GHz for maximum gain. Altogether, eight beams are needed to provide coverage extending over a ±14.5° angular sector.

articleTitle: Exact numerical solution of helmholtz's equation in dielectric gratings with arbitrary profiles
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: Based on an exact solution of the pertinent boundary-value problem, a method is presented for finding the electromagnetic fields scattered or guided by dielectric gratings having arbitrary profiles. This method unifies the treatment of both perpendicular (TE) and parallel (TM) polarization by using the Boundary Element Method (BEM). To illustrate the method, the results are presented for a four layer waveguide with trapezoidal grating.

articleTitle: The performance of a radio link for indoor communications at 29 Ghz
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: This paper focuses on the design of an indoor broadband radio system at 29 GHz with some emphasis on the effect of antennas on the availability of the system, for various cell sizes. The system has a maximum information bit rate of 155 Mb/sec and a maximum receiver noise figure of 8 dB. Channel measurements with antenna diversity were carried out during an earlier stage of the project at 2L6 GHz and 37.2 GHz. The resulting characterization provided knowledge of the parameters needed to evaluate the performance of the link. These included large-scale path-loss models which gave estimates of the power-law exponents and statistics of the received envelope. Transceiver characteristics and measured channel behavior as outlined above along with the different antenna types (omnidirectional and horn) and different antenna orientations determine the distribution of the received power across the cell, and thus the average availability. Practical configurations were investigated involving partial alignment or no alignment of the base station and portable antennas. Full antenna alignment was also examined for the purpose of comparison.

articleTitle: A fast robust quasi-newton algorithm for adaptive arrays
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: This paper outlines the development of a new type of digital adaptive-array algorithm for interference cancellation. It is fast in the sense that it requires only order-of-N computations per iteration and converges in a substantially fixed number of iterations (proportional to N) regardless of the signal scenario or geometry of the N-element array. The need for such algorithms arises in dynamic signal scenarios requiring spatial cancellation of co-channel interference, such as in military aircraft communications [1] and digital mobile-radio telephony [2, 3]. Existing order-of-N LMS (Least Mean Squares) algorithms are inadequate for such applications as they suffer from very slow modes of convergence. Ordinary RLS (Recursive Least Squares) algorithms converge much faster but require order-of-N operations per iteration which hampers their realization.

articleTitle: Rigorous analysis of pulse propagation on superconductor CPW
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: Transient propagation of Gaussian pulses on superconductive conductor-backed coplanar waveguides are investigated by a modified Finite Difference Time Domain method (FDTD). The two-fluid model is used to describe the superconductor. The frequency-dependent negative imaginary part of the conductivity is modeled with the FDTD by storing the electric field history. A variable mesh with second order accuracy is used to resolve the thin superconductor layer.

articleTitle: Modeling wave propagation for microcellular network
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: Modeling propagation in urban areas is fundamental for microcellular network design. The main difficulty in developing deterministic models is that propagation areas are both large in size and complex in shape. In this study, we focus on the power transmission characteristics of the wave propagation process and we divide the process into basic elements according to the geometrical characteristics of built up areas and the power transmission mechanisms of the different structures. As a starting point, propagation modeling of the street canyons is investigated. Propagation in a LOS street as well as propagation through a street intercrossing is illustrated.

articleTitle: Application of a new direct method to the repeated solution of general linear systems with modified equations
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: A new direct method for solving general systems of linear algebraic equations originated by the author is applied to the repealed solution of a given system when changes of some rows occur in the system matrix. Such repeated computations are needed in numerous practical problems, e.g. in various imaging devices (electromagnetic, acoustic, etc.) or in linear optimization. The solution method is based on using only one original equation at each main step of the algorithm independently of the rest of the equations, with no elimination of the unknowns and no backward substitution. This makes our solution procedure fundamentally different from and more efficient than those with Gaussian elimination, regarding storage requirement, pivoting, controlling the accuracy, and the amount of computation for special applications. A brief description of the principle of the method is the following.

articleTitle: Moment method dipole antenna analysis and its measurement
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: Cylindrical dipole antenna is the basic element in antenna and scattering analysis. Here, a symmetrical cylindrical dipole antenna analyzed and measured by, 1) Analyzed by MM (Moment Method) based on NEC (Numerical Electromagnetic Code), 2) Analyzed by a separate M M program based on PWS (Piece Wise Sinusoidal) basis and PWL (Piece Wise Linear) base function. 3) Measured a typical monopole over RF ground plane in the frequency range 100 MHz to 300 MHz in the resonance frequency by Vector Voltmeter hp 8405A. In measurement, a matrix error with five error module is considered. Four error module are belong to reflection measurement set up and one error is transition to antenna error. Direct measured data are together with error. Error at some region gives negative real part impedance. After the error deembeding, the measured data are in agreement with numerical analysis. In this paper the basic concept of the moment method together with numerical and measured data is presented. A five errors module deembedded in measurement.

articleTitle: Experimental determination of sky-wave interference in ground wave radars
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: Vertically directed radiation (ionospheric) properties of both the receiver and transmitter antennas used in the Cape Race Ground Wave Radar (GWR) are investigated experimentally as well as numerically. Using the radar system as the measurement tool, measurements were taken when a specially-built reference antenna in the form of a horizontal dipole replaced either the transmitting or the receiving antennas. Resulting ionospheric characteristics of the GWR system are compared favourably with those based on numerical codes, ICEPAC and the Numerical Electromagnetics Code (NEC). The results of these measurements provide a set of measurements which define the levels of skywave interference generated by the existing antenna system and will establish specifications for an antenna upgrade.

articleTitle: Cellular phones and humans-a neophyte outlook
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: A cellular phone is a portable radio that radiates 0.6 watt from an antenna located very close to the operator's head. Concern has been expressed as to whether a cellular phone is capable of inducing damaging field strengths inside the user's head. This paper reviews the application of electromagnetic modelling techniques using the finite-difference time-domain(FDTD) method to this problem. The construction of an FDTD model of the cellular phone and of the head is discussed. The relative permittivity and conductivity of biological tissue varies with frequency, and this paper reviews modifications of the FDTD method to handle such dispersive media. Some specific applications of measurement methods and of the FDTD method to the calculation of the amount of electromagnetic power delivered to the body are discussed.

articleTitle: Aperture coupled QUAD EMC super patch
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: The stacked quad EMC super patch with probe feeding was first proposed in [1] and a number of design results for personal communication terminals were provided in [2]. It has wide bandwidth of stacked microstrip antennas and higher gain due to the radiation of subarray. On the other hand, aperture coupling[3] can reduce the interaction between the antenna and feeding network, and the feed can be placed at a symmetric position to suppress cross polarization[4].

articleTitle: Computation and measurement of the resonant frequencies and Q factors of high-permittivity dielectric resonators
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: This paper describes the measurement and computation of the resonant frequencies and the associated Q factors of dielectric parallelepipeds made of high-permittivity, low-loss ceramic materials. The radar cross-section(RCS) is measured separately near each resonance peak with a fine frequency step. A curve-fitting method is used to accurately estimate the resonant frequency and the 3 dB bandwidth from the measured RCS. The calculation uses the finite-difference time-domain method to compute the initial portion of the backscattered field as a function of time, due to a Gaussian pulse plane wave. The transient response is then extended in time to zero value by Prony's method. and the Fourier transform is used to obtain the RCS as a function of frequency. The measured and computed resonant frequencies and Q factors are compared for parallelepiped resonators of permittivity 37.84 and 79.46.

articleTitle: 3D-TLM analysis of a via hole between microstrip and stripline for multilayer antennas
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: This paper presents the analysis of a via hole contact between a microstrip and stripline for potential applications in multilayer antennas. A full-wave analysis based on the 3D-TLM method is used to model the transition. The effect of the via and the clearance hole shape and size were discussed. Simulations obtained using this analysis were compared to the measured data.

articleTitle: Finite-difference time domain model of a coaxial probe
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: Input impedance of truncated coaxial cable is of considerable importance both from the calibration standard and non-destructive testing points of view. Significant effort has been expended in their analysis [1-3] in order to understand and exploit the fringing field effects. For a calibration standard knowledge of the fringing fields is essential to determine the additional frequency dependent capacitance at the aperture. In non-destructive testing the aperture reflection coefficient is related to the electrical properties of the terminating material. Advantages of this method of material measurement include little or no sample preparation, small sample size and a frequency range from DC to the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode cutoff since operation is in the TEM mode. These characteristics make the coaxial probe an ideal choice for many non-destructive measurements.

articleTitle: MHMIC technology applied to active integrated antennas
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: An active integrated antenna may be defined as a radiating element on which the current distribution along the structure may be altered in a controlled manner. The ability to control the current distribution along its structure is the unique feature of this class of antennas and gives it its primary advantage. With this ability, radiation characteristics such as pattern shape, axial ratio, and gain may all be controlled. An antenna configuration with integrated active devices has been developed [1]. The resultant topology is a microstrip transmission line configuration with cascade distributed amplifiers. This active antenna has been designed, modelled, fabricated, and its radiation characteristics measured. The above capabilities of controlling the radiation characteristics have been verified. The prototype active antenna utilized three packaged amplifiers and a microstrip transmission line on a Duroid substrate (ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>=2.94) (Figure 1). To facilitate the fabrication of active integrated antennas, the application of Miniature Hybrid Microwave Integrated Circuit (MHMIC) technology was investigated.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of a large TEM cell
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: A wire grid model has been used to numerically model a 6 m long TEM cell with the Numerical Electromagnetic Code (NEC) [1]. Difficulties in modelling a solid metal structure as a series of wires are discussed. The onset of the various TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nmp</inf> and TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nmp</inf> modes and their overall field distributions are predicted. Comparison of the TEM field distribution is made to that determined by an independent Moment Method solution [2]. Field magnitudes established by the two methods (in the central portion of the cell) deviate by less than 2 dB, a value which is adequate for most EMC testing.

articleTitle: On the calculation of canonical bodies using the MMP code
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: The MMP modeling of different scattering structures is discussed. It is shown, that highly accurate near and farfield simulations are possible, not only for simple academic structures such as spheres or cubes, but also for a multiturn helical wire of finite thickness and an absorbing ferrite cylindre placed on a cable. Although the amount of calculation increases when edges or tips are present, rather small radii of curvature may be treated using (curved or straight) line multipoles.

articleTitle: Raised microstrip antenna array for marine MSAT
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: Marine MSAT requires an antenna array that functions in the 1525MHz to 1660.5MHz frequency band to be placed on sea going vessels. The gain of the overall array should be 14.1dBiC minimum. The implementation chosen is a right-hand circularly polarized microstrip array of four elements.

articleTitle: A novel double-layer microstrip bandpass filter
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: This paper presents a new type of microstrip bandpass filter. It is realized in a double-layer configuration, as shown in fig. 1. This design makes use of the vertical dimension to achieve a size reduction over conventional microstrip parallel coupled bandpass filters [1]. These conventional filters have significant overall widths because the widths depend on the number of coupling sections. Also, they require very small spacings between the parallel coupled resonators which may be difficult to achieve in a fabrication process. The proposed new filter, with the overlaid resonators, is much narrower in overall width and does not require close spacings between resonators. An earlier study [2] investigated a modified parallel coupled microstrip bandpass filter with its topology somewhat similar to the one here. However, it is still a single layer structure and therefore the tight spacings between resonators are still essential.

articleTitle: Impedance method — Application and limitations in modelling cellulor interactions of magnetic fields
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: The impedance method, which is a circuit representation of the finite difference method for quasi-static problems is applied to model induced electric fields and currents in biological cells exposed to 60 Hz magnetic fields. Two simplified representations of actual preparations used in laboratory studies are considered. These are: low and high density suspension of cells in a conductive medium. and a monolayer of cells connected by gap-junctions.

articleTitle: A review of irregular conformal meshes in FDTD
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: There are many ways to apply the finite difference method to the time domain Maxwell equations. One of the first applications was the time-space centered algorithm formulated by Yee [1] which is now usually refered to as the finite difference time domain (FDTD) method. In this paper we will be using the term FDTD in the more general sense to include any other finite difference technique which can be applied to solve the Maxwell equations. Traditionally the use of the FDTD method to solve electromagnetic interaction problems has been aproached with the view of making the geometrical problem fit the algorithm. The computational space defined using Yee's algorithm is a Cartesian grid and the physical structures are embedded in the space such that their boundaries are aligned with the computational grid. In the case of a complex shaped object, the surface is approximated by stepped edges [2, 3, 4] in order to preserve the rectangular computational grid. This approach has its limitations and the errors introduced by using it have been analysed elsewhere [5].

articleTitle: Low profile microstrip antenna for airborne applications
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: Automatic picture transmission of real-time meteorological conditions to aircraft via satellite is receiving increasing attention in numerous applications, from improving flight efficiency to search and rescue. Currently, they are a number of satellites that provide such a capability. In Canada, most of the required information is in the northern regions and the best satellite information is not from geostationary satellites, but from polar orbiting weather satellites. They are the United States NOAA Satellites, Russian Meteor and Chinese Fen Yung Satellites. Their operating frequency bands are listed in Table 1 and cover from 137.3 MHz to 137.795 MHz. These spacecrafts scan the northern and polar regions every 101 minutes and have resolution of about one mile. In addition, since these satellites are at lower orbits of 400–600 miles, the signal attenuation is not to the same degree on geostationary satellites. The low operating frequency of 137 MHz also reduces the path loss attenuation. Consequently, the real time images can be received using low gain omnidirectional antennas.

articleTitle: A comparison of two new iterative procedures for microwave imaging
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: In recent years, the investigation of inverse scattering problems in the area of microwave imaging has been performed mainly by applying iterative algorithms. The method based on me Born approximation [1] and the method using a Newton-type iterative algorithm [2] are two typical iterative methods currently being employed. An improved technique based on the equivalent current reconstruction has been proposed by the authors [3],[4]. In the new technique, at eacb iteration step, the permittivity profile of the object determined by using either the Born approximation or the Newton iterative algorithm is used to update the equivalent current distribution. Then a better evaluation of the permittivity distribution is obtained by using the updated current. The new method provides better results than those corresponding to the existing methods mentioned above. At the same time, it is found that the convergence of the new iterative procedure, when employing the Born approximation or the Newton algorithm, appears to be quite different in different situations and the selection of the optimum technique to be used in the proposed method becomes important for an efficient imaging. In this paper, results derived by the proposed method, based on me two iterative procedures, are compared for the case of multiple illuminations. It is shown that the Born iterative procedure is more advantageous for continuous profiles, while the Newton iterative algorithm is more suitable for profiles with discontinuities.

articleTitle: A compact high gain planar microstrip array for mobile satellite communication
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: This paper describes the design and development of a low profile phased array suitable for INMARSAT Standard-M vehicular satellite communications. The array consists of twelve dual layer elements symmetrically positioned on a circular disk. The lower microstrip patches are fed directly to radiate right-handed circular polarization while the upper patches act as parasitic elements. Optimization has been carried out to improve the impedance bandwidth and to enhance the radiation characteristics. The array is designed to yield a fixed beam in the middle of the required elevation coverage region and is mechanically rotated in the azimuth plane. Its performance has been characterized within the frequency bands 1530–1559 MHz for receive and 1626.5–1660.5 MHz for transmit.

articleTitle: Numerical methods in bioelectromagnetics at microwave frequencies
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: Computer modeling and numerical techniques provide valuable results in the area of bioelectromagnetics. In this paper, advantages and limitations of three numerical techniques, namely the method of moments (MoM), the finite-difference time domain method (FDTD) and the spherical wave expansion functions are addressed and discussed. Examples of the results obtained with the FDTD for the interaction of a half-wave dipole with dielectric bodies at cellular telephony frequencies (840, 900, 1500 and 1800 MHz) at distances of 25 mm and closer are presented. Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) computations are given for different dielectric bodies and especially for a 3-D model of the human eye within its bony orbit for continuous wave exposure. It is found that computed energy deposition values are in excess of ANSI's SAR value for an uncontrolled environment of 1.6 W/kg.

articleTitle: A variable feed line gap discontinuity for a multi-layer patch antenna
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: A multi-layer patch antenna that is fed by a gap discontinuity within a microstrip feed line is investigated. The feed line is located on the lower layer of the structure, while a rectangular patch is centred above the gap discontinuity on the upper layer. The structure is analyzed by the moment method in the spatial domain and employs a matched load simulation technique. Comparison with experimental results indicates that this numerical approach accurately predicts me antenna's characteristics and also presents a useful model for design purposes.

articleTitle: Investigation of the reflective properties of double layered periodic structures
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: A proper Green's function is developed to study the reflective properties of structures composed of two layers of periodic structures printed on the two interfaces of a dielectric slab. Implementation of periodic structures composed of cell elements of different sizes and/or shapes on the two interfaces of a dielectric slab leads to certain interesting characteristics such as: decreasing the angular sensitivity of the structure, translation of the resonance frequency and creation of new resonances. The results of computer simulations that demonstrate such phenomena are presented.

articleTitle: Reversibility, information-preservation, and the presence of instabilities in time-domain numerical methods
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: Vichniac has stated that “Exact numerical reversibility yields instability in the presence of an attractor” [1]. Vichniac's statement relates the reversibility of an algorithm (i.e., its ability to preserve the information encoded in its initial conditions) to the dynamics of an attractor. In this paper, the relevance of Vichniac's statement to the time-domain numerical methods applied to model electromagnetic phenomena is assessed. Relevant practical problems include the development of time-domain differential-equation based numerical methods, and the application of local absorbing boundary conditions. The general approach described in this paper complements the traditional Von Neumann method for stability analysis. It is anticipated that the concepts introduced in this paper will be applicable to situations which involve time-domain modelling and unanticipated instabilities.

articleTitle: Design of low profile cavity backed slot antenna
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
abstract: The general problem of coupling through apertures has applications in slotted arrays, directional couplers, microstrip lines, etc. Numerous references are available in the literature, most of which use the Green's theorem to reduce the problem to an integral equation for the unknown tangential electric field in the aperture. Of these, the moment method is especially attractive because it inherently deals with apertures of arbitrary shape and size. It has been used extensively to examine the problems of two waveguides coupled through a rectangular slot, using pulse basis functions and point matching. In this paper, we apply equivalence principle and the generalized network formulation [1] to model the tangential electric field of arbitrary apertures backed by a rectangular waveguide or cavity, in terms of equivalent magnetic current. The result is an integral equation for the unknown aperture current. This integral equation is then reduced to a matrix equation using the method of moments.

articleTitle: A high temperature superconductor filter/low-noise amplifier MIC
publicationTitle: Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 1994]
